prompt: Use case: historical-scene. ONE production animation storyboard sprite sheet for an Age-of-Sail historical exploration game. EXACTLY 4 equal columns by 4 equal rows: sixteen landscape panels, no extra panels. Request overall 2304x1024 wide sheet, each individual cell 576x256 ultrawide. Perfect boundaries at exact quarter lines, edge-to-edge without margins or gutters, no border, labels, numbers, writing or captions. Realistic finely painted miniature documentary cinematography, consistent coherent main site in all panels; no graphic overlays. Left-to-right then top-to-bottom sequence. Subject: TODAIJI GREAT BUDDHA HALL in Nara, Japan, as the reconstructed medieval Kamakura-period wooden hall would stand around 1480, before the 1567 fire, a broad monumental timber hall with an expansive dark gray tiled double-eaved roof, deep timber bracketwork, red-brown pillars, open front doors and stone base in green wooded temple precinct; broad and stately medieval facade, not the narrower 1709 version and no ornate later central curved gable. Inside: enormous dark bronze seated Vairocana Buddha on a lotus pedestal, right palm raised, left palm open on lap, curled hair, great circular gold-bronze halo, tall natural timber pillars. One massive pillar has a small square opening at floor level. Sequence panels: 1 small miniature foundation and timber framing on wood table, 2 timber columns rise, 3 roof beams installed, 4 double-eaved tiled roof placed, 5 completed miniature hall and precinct, 6 match cut to real full-scale hall circa 1480 in green Nara landscape, 7 approach through open timber doors, 8 wide interior showing seated bronze Buddha and towering pillars, 9 side interior with tiny floor-level square opening in one pillar, 10 view out from hall to temple court, 11 elevated frontal three-quarter view of whole hall by afternoon, 12 another orbit bearing showing long roof and wooden side wall, 13 golden sunset over temple roof, 14 tranquil moonlight among trees, 15 pale dawn mist, 16 clear morning final panorama of the entire medieval hall. Maintain same architecture across panels, medieval historically grounded interpretation, no modern tourist railings, signs, wires, cars, skyscrapers, glass doors or electric lamps, no Chinese-style pagoda replacing the hall.
